name: Mulberry (Crayola)
lede: Mulberry (Crayola) is Crayola's own reddish-purple take on the plain color [[mulberry]], close enough to it to read as almost the same shade.

sections.title: A brand's own variant
sections.body:
Our library credits this name to Crayola's own color list, distinguishing the brand's swatch from the plain color word [[mulberry]] it variantly builds on [1]. No first-recorded date survives in the sources we checked [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary's nearest block is "strong reddish purple," 7.6 units from that block's centre, a looser match than most named colors get [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is the plain [[mulberry|Mulberry]] itself, only 3.2 units away and read as almost the same color [2]. [[red-violet-crayola|Red-Violet (Crayola)]] sits 3.7 units out, also almost the same, and [[pale-magenta|Purplish Pink]] 4.4 units out [2]. [[frostbite|Frostbite]] sits further out at 5.5 units, more vivid [2]. Measured in LCH it reads lightness 52, chroma 58, a strongly saturated magenta-purple [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries this exact color covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes a gap in this particular archive, not a claim that the shade never appears in art; a saturated brand color this close to its name's own swatch is close to screen-only [3].
